extracted.intended_audience: Users of the Magma computer algebra system (students, researchers, practitioners) learning to write Magma code and perform algebraic computations
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory Magma language and workflow guidance: how to compute invariants, Molien series, Galois groups, and basic Magma programming idioms (printing, assignment, identifiers, booleans, where-construction, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute conjugacy classes as orbits under conjugation action when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing conjugacy classes for large matrix groups, find the classes C as orbits under conjugation action (i.e., Classes(G: Al := "Action")) because the default method may be much slower for this group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call Classes(G: Al := "Action") to compute conjugacy classes and store them for subsequent calculations. Example: C := Classes(G: Al := "Action"); #C;

rubrics_metrics.name: Write Molien series both as a rational function and power series
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the Molien series MS<t> := MolienSeries(G) to obtain a rational function and then expand it as a power series to inspect dimensions of invariant spaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PowerSeriesRing(IntegerRing(), N) and coerce MS into it to get coefficients up to desired order. Example: P<x> := PowerSeriesRing(IntegerRing(),200); P ! MS;

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret Molien series denominator to deduce candidate degrees of primary invariants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Molien series can be written in the form (1 + t^m) / ((1 − t^{s1})···(1 − t^{sd})), so the exponents s1,...,sd in the denominator indicate possible degrees for primary invariants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partially factor the denominator by dividing out factors (1 − t^k) successively, determining each k from the degree of the first non-constant term and verifying the product equals the denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct invariants of candidate degrees using ReynoldsOperator and InvariantsOfDegree
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute explicit invariant polynomials of the degrees suggested by the Molien series: use ReynoldsOperator for a base invariant and InvariantsOfDegree to produce linearly independent invariants of a given degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example workflow: P<x1,..,xd> := PolynomialRing(K,d); i8 := ReynoldsOperator(x1^8, G); L24 := InvariantsOfDegree(G,P,24,2); InvariantsOfDegree internally calls ReynoldsOperator efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify primary invariants by showing the ideal they generate is zero-dimensional
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ideal generated by the candidate invariants is zero-dimensional and the Hilbert series numerator equals the expected product (∏ (1 − t^{si})), then those invariants are primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use HilbertGroebnerBasis(L, D) (Hilbert-driven Buchberger algorithm). A return of true indicates the ideal is zero-dimensional. Check numerator equals (1 − t^{s1})···(1 − t^{sd}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Check factorization identity when deducing denominator factors
rubrics_metrics.description: After dividing the denominator by successive (1 − t^k) factors, verify that the product of those factors equals the original denominator D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute D eq (1 - t^8)*(1 - t^24)*(1 - t^24)*(1 - t^40); expect true. This confirms the chosen degrees are consistent with the Molien denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use cyclotomic/number fields for group constructions when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct groups over appropriate number fields (e.g., CyclotomicField(8)) when matrix entries require roots of unity or other algebraic numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: K<zeta> := CyclotomicField(8); G := MatrixGroup<4,K | ... >. Choose the field so group generators are defined naturally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute Galois groups via splitting fields and explicit permutation action
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an explicit action of the Galois group, construct the splitting field, factor the relevant polynomials over it, obtain roots, and determine permutations of conjugates induced by automorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workflow: N := NumberField(f); extend to splitting field M; A := AbsoluteField(M); factor DefiningPolynomial(A); collect roots C; build polynomials P representing conjugates; produce permutations I and subgroup H := sub< Sym(n) | I >.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use intrinsic GaloisGroup and verify conjugacy with constructed group
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also call GaloisGroup(DefiningPolynomial(A)) to get the Galois group; verify it is conjugate to an explicitly constructed permutation group using IsConjugate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: G := GaloisGroup(DefiningPolynomial(A)); fl, el := IsConjugate(Sym(n), G, H); expect fl = true and el a relabeling permutation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find subgroups and corresponding subfields via subgroup lattice and traces
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Subgroups(H) to explore subgroup conjugacy classes, select a subgroup K, form its automorphisms on the field A, and use traces (e.g., trace of a^3) to produce generators for subfields corresponding to K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: S := Subgroups(H); K := S[i]'subgroup; J := [ hom< A -> A | C[1^k] > : k in K ]; tra := &+[ h(C[1]^3) : h in J ]; then MinimalPolynomial(tra) reveals the subfield.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use print to produce output; print optional interactively but required in functions/procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The print-statement prints evaluated expressions. In interactive runs the token print may be omitted, but print is mandatory inside functions, procedures and intrinsics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: print expression; or print expr1, expr2, ...; Omit print when working interactively for brevity, but include it in program definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print multiple expressions separated by commas; spaces optional but aid legibility
rubrics_metrics.description: print expression, expression, ... will evaluate and print several expressions. Spaces around operators and commas are optional; use them to improve readability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: print a, b; or interactively: a, b; Both work; prefer spaces for legibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard operators and be mindful of precedence; use parentheses to control order
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma uses * for multiplication, ^ or ↑ for exponentiation, / for exact division, and div and mod for quotient and remainder. Operator precedence follows algebraic conventions; parentheses force evaluation order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (x^5 + 4) div (x^2 - 3*x + 1); use parentheses for clarity in complex expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrinsics naming and usage: most intrinsics begin with a capital letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Intrinsic functions (pre-defined functions) are invoked by name followed by parentheses; most intrinsic names start with a capital letter (e.g., Factorial(n), GCD(a,b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an intrinsic has no arguments, parentheses are required. Avoid redefining intrinsics as identifiers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strings use double quotes; use printf for formatted output
rubrics_metrics.description: Enclose text in double quotation marks "" to print explanatory text with values. For advanced formatting use printf (see chapter on formatting).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "Factorial of five is", Factorial(5); prints accompanying text and value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose meaningful identifier names and follow naming rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifiers may contain letters, digits and underscore, but cannot start with a digit. Prefer longer meaningful names (e.g., len, product). Magma is case-sensitive and reserved words cannot be identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assigning values to intrinsic names. The special identifier _ is the throwaway identifer and should not be used as an ordinary name. See reserved words list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspect assigned identifiers and values with ShowIdentifiers/ShowValues
rubrics_metrics.description: ShowIdentifiers() prints a list of currently assigned identifier names; ShowValues() prints names together with their values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when many assignments have been made or to debug environment state. Example: ShowValues();

rubrics_metrics.name: Free memory by deleting large/unwanted values with delete and test assignment with assigned
rubrics_metrics.description: Use delete identifier, ... to remove stored values and free workspace memory. Use assigned identifier to test whether an identifier currently has a value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After delete the identifier becomes unassigned. Example: assigned zxcv; delete zxcv; assigned zxcv;

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment semantics: := stores the evaluated value, not the expression
rubrics_metrics.description: The simple assignment ident := expression evaluates the right-hand side and stores the resulting value; subsequent changes to other identifiers do not retroactively affect stored values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: V := L*B*H; later changing L does not change V. Use temporary identifiers when swapping values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use mutation assignment (◦:=) for efficient in-place updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Mutation assignment ident ◦:= expression mutates the existing value of ident by applying operator ◦ with the expression; it is often more efficient than ident := ident ◦ expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common forms: d *:= 53; which is equivalent to d := d * 53 but may avoid copies and be faster.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand multi-valued expressions and multiple assignment rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Some functions return multiple values. If assigned to a single identifier only the first (principal) value is computed; multiple identifiers on the left receive successive return values. Use _ to discard unwanted returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful with performance: avoid requesting non-principal return values unless needed (e.g., SmithForm returns S quickly but P,Q are expensive). Syntax: q,r := Quotrem(26,4); _, r := Quotrem(100,13);

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the where-construction for local temporary bindings
rubrics_metrics.description: The expression where identifier is expression provides a temporary binding of identifier limited to that expression, avoiding global assignments and side-effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Syntax: f := d*(d+1)*(d^2+5) where d is x^5 - 4*x^3 + 17; Scope of d is only the where-construction; it does not alter outer d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coerce numbers explicitly when needed and be aware of numeric parents
rubrics_metrics.description: Integers have arbitrary precision; rationals are fraction objects; reals and complex numbers have fixed or free precision depending on settings. Coerce integers into a field with RationalField()!, RealField()!, ComplexField()! or by literal forms (e.g., 37.0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Parent(...) to inspect the parent magma. Example: Parent(rat37) is Rational Field. Use explicit coercion with the ! operator when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean operators and short-circuit (conditional) evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Relational operators eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge test relations; Boolean operators not, and, or, xor operate as expected. and/or are conditionally evaluated (left-to-right short-circuiting), which can prevent errors or expensive computations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit short-circuiting: false and expensive_expression avoids evaluating the expensive part. Beware that naively writing e.g., 5/2 and false will error unless the left operand is a Boolean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean-testing intrinsics: Is*/Has*/Are* patterns and multi-value boolean returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Many property tests are named Is... or Has... and return true/false. Some Boolean functions return additional useful information when true (e.g., IsSquare(a) returns true and the positive square root).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multiple assignment to capture extra return values: sq, sqroot := IsSquare(144); only sqroot assigned if sq is true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting conventions: block and line comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Use /* ... */ for block comments (not nested) and // for line comments to document code. Comments are ignored by Magma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comments to explain purpose and logic. Remember block comments cannot be nested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recall previously printed values using $n notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Values printed by recent print-statements can be recalled: $1 holds the list of values from the most recent print, $2 from the next most recent, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use $1, $2 ... to reuse outputs without recomputing. Note the number after $ must be a literal integer.
